title: Predicting when tabular neural models beat trees
known: Earlier benchmarks connected neural/tree differences to inductive biases and dataset meta-features. TabPFN reports strong small-data performance from synthetic-task pretraining, and a follow-up interprets it through approximate Bayesian inference and adaptation to statistical structure.
question: Can measurable dataset properties and pretraining-prior mismatch predict the neural-versus-tree frontier under explicit amortized pretraining, inference and tuning budgets?
boundary: The older premise that trees dominate is already overturned on important reported benchmarks. The remaining question must compare current pretrained models, amortized pretraining cost and deployment cost, and audit prior mismatch and dataset overlap.
decisive_test: Change nuisance features, orientation, irregularity and sample size independently; freeze selection on new domains with equal total tuning cost.
